Agree là động từ (không phải tính từ) và: Agree is a verb (not an adjective) and a stative verb → I agree. "am agree" uses be with a verb; "am agreeing" uses the continuous with a stative verb; "agreeing" has no main verb.

Although / because nối hai mệnh đề trong: Although / because join two clauses in ONE sentence; however / therefore join TWO sentences. Don't use although and but in the same sentence, and don't write "despite of".
Although và but không dùng cùng nhau tro: Although and but are not used together in one sentence.
Amount of đi với danh từ không đếm được;: Amount of goes with uncountable nouns; tourists is countable so keep number.
An trước nguyên âm (theo phát âm, không: An before a vowel sound (by pronunciation, not spelling)
Anh-Anh: gấp đôi -l sau nguyên âm đơn: British English: double -l after a single vowel
Another chỉ đi với danh từ số ít; số nhi: Another goes only with a singular noun; for plurals use other.
As / since: lý do người nghe đã biết, th: As / since: a reason the listener already knows, usually at the start of the sentence
As if + quá khứ hoàn thành: trái với sự: As if + past perfect: contrary to what really happened
As if + quá khứ đơn: tưởng tượng, trái v: As if + past simple: imagined, contrary to the present
As if + thì bình thường: điều có thể đún: As if + normal tense: possibly true (based on evidence)
As if – không thật trong quá khứ: As if – unreal in the past
As if – không thật ở hiện tại: As if – unreal in the present
Asleep chỉ đứng sau động từ; trước danh: Asleep comes only after a verb; before a noun use sleeping.
At 10 o'clock last night → quá khứ tiếp: At 10 o'clock last night → past continuous; you takes were. was does not go with you; did and are are the wrong tense/structure with doing.
At the moment → hiện tại tiếp diễn bị độ: At the moment → present continuous passive: is being built. is built does not show an action in progress; has built and builds are active.
Avoid is always followed by V-ing.
Ba loại liên từ: kết hợp (FANBOYS: for,: Three types of conjunction: coordinating (FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so), correlative (both…and, either…or, neither…nor, not only…but also) and subordinating (because, although, if, when, while…). With comma rules.
Ba tính từ song song: spacious, modern,: Three parallel adjectives: spacious, modern, comfortable. "it is comfortable" breaks the parallelism; comfortably is an adverb; comfort is a noun.
Ba động từ hiện tại đơn song song: inspi: Three parallel present simple verbs: inspire, explain, give. giving, to give, gave are not parallel with inspire, explain.
Band 7 yêu cầu “a variety of complex str: Band 7 requires “a variety of complex structures” and “frequent error-free sentences”. One correct complex sentence is worth more than three faulty ones, so vary your structures but keep control.
Be going to – dự đoán có bằng chứng ngay: Be going to – a prediction based on present evidence
Be going to – dự định đã có từ trước: Be going to – an intention already made before speaking
Be quiet là trạng thái, không phải hành: Be quiet is a state, not a repeated action, so would is not used.
Because + mệnh đề ↔ because of / due to: Because + clause ↔ because of / due to + noun phrase
Because of + cụm danh từ, không + mệnh đ: Because of + noun phrase, not + clause. Or use Because the government invested more…
Belong chỉ sự sở hữu, là động từ trạng t: Belong expresses possession and is a stative verb, so it takes the simple form.
Biến một gốc từ thành danh từ, động từ,: Turn a root into a noun, verb, adjective or adverb with suffixes, and change meaning with prefixes such as un-, dis-, mis-, over-, re-. A key skill for gap-fill tasks in Listening and Reading.
Biến động từ/tính từ thành danh từ (deci: Turn verbs/adjectives into nouns (decide → decision, rise → a rise) to pack a whole clause into a noun phrase – making sentences concise, objective and academic.
When you know it is unreal → shift the tense back (were).

Biểu đồ có dự báo tương lai → will / be: Chart with future projections → will / be expected to / will have V3
Biểu đồ có năm trong quá khứ → quá khứ đ: Chart with past years → past simple
Biểu đồ trong đề đã xác định với người đ: The chart in the task is already identified for the reader, so use The. A/An is for the first mention of any chart; no article is wrong because pie chart is singular countable.
Both (cả hai) – either (một trong hai) –: Both (the two) – either (one of two) – neither (not one of the two)
Both + N số nhiều, hoặc both of + the/my: Both + plural N, or both of + the/my + plural N.

By + mốc quá khứ (By 2000) → quá khứ hoà: By + past point in time (By 2000) → past perfect had + V3 → had reached. has reached is present perfect; "had reach" lacks V3; "was reaching" does not show completion before the point.
By + mốc tương lai (By 2050) trong dự bá: By + future point (By 2050) in a projection → future perfect will have + V3 → will have doubled. doubles, doubled and has doubled do not express completion before a future point.
By + mốc tương lai nhấn mạnh việc hoàn t: By + future point in time emphasises completion before that point → future perfect.
By + mốc tương lai, hoàn tất trước mốc →: By + future point, completed before that point → will have found. will find does not stress completion before the point; will be finding is in progress; have found is present perfect.
By the time + hiện tại đơn; mệnh đề chín: By the time + present simple; main clause will have + V3. Don't use will after By the time; "will have start" lacks V3; "has started" is the wrong tense.
By the time + quá khứ đơn → mệnh đề chín: By the time + past simple → past perfect in the main clause. destroys and has destroyed are the wrong tense; destroyed does not show it happened before the firefighters arrived.
Bị cấm (strictly forbidden) → mustn't. d: Forbidden (strictly forbidden) → mustn't. don't have to and needn't mean not necessary (not forbidden); ought to is advice about what you should do.
Bị động tường thuật: It + is + V3 + that: Reporting passive: It + is + V3 + that + clause → It is expected that… "It expects" is active and has the wrong meaning; "They are expected" must be followed by to V; "Is expected" lacks the subject It.
Bị động: giữ nguyên tiểu từ sau V3: Passive: keep the particle after V3
Bỏ đại từ khi là tân ngữ: Omitting the pronoun when it is the object
Bốn cách đổi mệnh đề → cụm danh từ: (1): Four ways to turn a clause into a noun phrase: (1) adjective + noun (it was cold → the cold weather); (2) possessive adjective + noun (he was absent → his absence); (3) V-ing when the subject is the SAME (she was tired → being tired); (4) the fact that + clause – the safe way when you cannot find a noun.
Bốn cấu trúc diễn đạt lời khuyên, sự ưu: Four structures for expressing advice, preference and urgency – each is followed by a different verb form, and some use the past tense to talk about the present.
Bổ nghĩa cho danh từ increase nên cần tí: It modifies the noun increase, so the adjective dramatic is needed. dramatically is an adverb; drama is a noun; dramatise is a verb.
Bổ nghĩa cho tính từ so sánh higher → tr: Modifying the comparative adjective higher → the adverb slightly. slight is an adjective; "very" does not modify comparatives (it must be much / far higher); more duplicates the comparative form.
Bổ nghĩa cho động từ fell nên cần trạng: It modifies the verb fell, so the adverb steadily is needed. steady is an adjective; steadiness is a noun; "more steady" is a comparative adjective, which doesn't modify a verb.
Bổ nghĩa cho động từ has risen → trạng t: Modifying the verb has risen → the adverb significantly. significant is an adjective; significance is a noun; signify is a verb.
Bổ nghĩa cho động từ increased phải dùng: To modify the verb increased you must use an adverb.
Bộ từ mô tả xu hướng cần thuộc ở cả hai: Learn the trend vocabulary in both forms: slight/slightly, gradual/gradually, steady/steadily, sharp/sharply, dramatic/dramatically, considerable/considerably.
Can không có dạng nguyên mẫu hay V3, nên: Can has no infinitive or V3 form, so after will, have, might… you must use be able to: will be able to, have been able to, might be able to.
Children đã là số nhiều bất quy tắc (khô: Children is already an irregular plural (not ending in -s) → add 's.
Chuyển lời nói trực tiếp sang gián tiếp: Convert direct speech to indirect speech by backshifting tenses, changing pronouns, time and place expressions, and choosing a suitable reporting verb.
Chênh lệch chỉ 1 điểm phần trăm (50% → 5: A difference of only 1 percentage point (50% → 51%) → slightly (a little). considerably, dramatically and far all describe a large increase, which doesn't match the figures.

Chúc ai điều có thể xảy ra → hope. Lỗi d: Wishing someone something that may happen → hope. Learners often use wish where hope is needed.

Chỉ giữ \"by + tác nhân\" khi nó mang th: Keep "by + agent" only when it carries new or important information: The novel was written by a 17-year-old student.
Chỉ mục đích bằng động từ: to + V, không: Express purpose with a verb: to + V, not for + V.
Chỉ ngoại động từ (có tân ngữ) mới chuyể: Only transitive verbs (with an object) can become passive. Verbs such as happen, occur, arrive, die, rise, fall have no passive form.
Chỉ sở hữu (chiếc xe của người phụ nữ) d: Only possession (the woman's car) takes whose. who/whom refer to people, not possession; which refers to things.

Chồng chất quá nhiều từ thận trọng làm c: Piling up too many hedging words makes a sentence weak and wordy. One is enough.
Chủ ngữ là \"the number\" (con số) → độn: The subject is "the number" (a figure) → singular verb.
Chủ ngữ là V-ing hoặc mệnh đề → số ít: A subject that is V-ing or a clause → singular
Chủ ngữ số nhiều (they, we, you) đi với: Plural subjects (they, we, you) take were, not was.
Chủ ngữ và tân ngữ là cùng người (teenag: Subject and object are the same people (teenagers) → reflexive pronoun themselves. them refers to other people; theirs and their are possessive forms.
Chủ động, cùng lúc / lý do: Active, at the same time / reason
Coherence and Cohesion đánh giá cả độ ch: Coherence and Cohesion assesses the accuracy of linking words too. Vary them: although/despite for concession, whereas for comparison in Task 1, so that/in order to for solutions in Task 2.
Comma splice: không được nối hai câu độc: Comma splice: you cannot join two independent clauses with just a comma. Use which, a full stop or a semicolon.
Could have V3 còn có nghĩa \"lẽ ra đã có: Could have V3 also means "was able to but didn't": You could have asked me for help.
Criteria đã là số nhiều (số ít: criterio: Criteria is already plural (singular: criterion), so no extra s.
Càng…càng: The + so sánh hơn …, the + so: The more…, the more…: The + comparative …, the + comparative … Earlier lacks the; The earliest is a superlative; "As earlier" is the wrong structure.
Các thành phần nối bằng and, or, but, bo: Items joined with and, or, but, both…and, not only…but also must have the same grammatical form; in comparisons you must compare two things of the same kind.
Các từ phủ định như never, rarely, seldo: Negative words such as never, rarely, seldom, hardly ever are not used together with not: I never eat fast food (not I don't never eat).
Các từ “bẫy” luôn không đếm được: advice: “Trap” words that are always uncountable: advice, information, research, equipment, furniture, luggage, homework, knowledge, news, traffic, accommodation. Don't add -s and don't use a/an.
Các động từ hay dùng: say, think, believ: Common verbs: say, think, believe, know, report, expect, consider, estimate, claim, allege. With estimate, pattern 1 is usual: It is estimated that 40% of…

Câu \"Có nhiều người…\" tiếng Việt → The: In some languages "there is/are" is expressed with the verb "have" or with no subject. In English, use There are many people who… or Many people…. Don't use "It has" or "Have" to mean "there is".
Câu bắt đầu bằng Which mà không gắn với: A sentence beginning with Which that is not attached to a main clause is a fragment.
Câu bị động (be + V3) đưa đối tượng chịu: The passive (be + V3) makes the affected thing the subject; it is very common in academic writing and IELTS Writing.
Câu chính dùng động từ thường ở quá khứ: A main clause with an ordinary verb in the past → the tag is didn't.
Câu chính khẳng định với have (have book: An affirmative main clause with have (have booked) → a negative tag with the same auxiliary: haven't you? didn't/don't use the wrong auxiliary; have you does not become negative.
Câu chẻ What + S + V + is… → What the go: Cleft sentence What + S + V + is… → What the government should do is… That, It, Which do not begin a noun clause lacking an object like this.
Câu chẻ nhấn mạnh người làm chủ ngữ dùng: A cleft sentence emphasising a person as the subject uses who (or that). which refers to things; what is not used in this cleft; whom cannot be a subject.
Câu cảm thán với danh từ: What + a/an +: Exclamation with a noun: What + a/an + adjective + noun (+ S + V)! → What an interesting talk it was!
Câu cảm thán: tự nhiên trong Speaking, t: Exclamatory: natural in Speaking, avoid in academic Writing
Câu hỏi Speaking Part 1 như \"How long h: Speaking Part 1 questions such as "How long have you been living in your hometown?" are best answered with this very tense. It shows grammatical accuracy with for/since.
Câu hỏi Wh- với động từ thường cần trợ đ: Wh- questions with ordinary verbs need the auxiliary do/does/did.
Câu hỏi Yes/No khi tường thuật → whether: A reported Yes/No question → whether/if. that is for statements; what is for Wh- questions; do does not appear in an indirect question.
Câu hỏi chủ ngữ: who/what làm chủ ngữ →: Subject questions: who/what as the subject → no do/does/did
Câu hỏi có/không gián tiếp (liệu có kịp: An indirect yes/no question (whether it will be on time) uses whether → whether the project will be finished. what and which need a missing element in the clause; "that if" is a wrong structure.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp dùng trật tự câu kể (S: Indirect questions use statement word order (S + V), with no inversion of the auxiliary.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp dùng trật tự khẳng địn: Indirect questions use statement word order, with no does.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp giữ trật tự câu kể: S: Indirect questions keep statement word order: S + V.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp lùi thì và không đảo n: Indirect questions are backshifted and have no inversion: where + S + V2 → where I worked. "do work" and "did work" keep the auxiliary of the direct question; "work did" has the wrong word order.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp → trật tự S + V: the e: Indirect question → S + V word order: the exam starts. "does the exam start" and "starts the exam" keep question word order; "the exam does start" has an unnecessary does.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp: S + V, lùi thì → the: Indirect question: S + V, backshifted → the train left. "did leave" and "does leave" keep the auxiliary; "leaves it" is the wrong tense and has an extra it.
Câu hỏi gián tiếp: lịch sự, không đảo, k: Indirect questions: polite, no inversion, no do
Câu hỏi gián tiếp: wh- + S + V (không đả: Indirect question: wh- + S + V (no inversion) → where the library is. "where is the library" keeps direct-question order; "where does" has an unnecessary auxiliary; "the library where is" has the wrong order.
Câu hỏi tường thuật KHÔNG còn dấu hỏi và: Reported questions no longer have a question mark and do NOT invert the auxiliary: He asked where the station WAS (not "where was the station?").
Câu hỏi tường thuật dùng trật tự câu khẳ: Reported questions use statement word order and drop did.
Câu hỏi về quá khứ phải được trả lời bằn: A question about the past must be answered in the past; repeating the wrong tense costs marks in Grammatical Range and Accuracy.
Câu hỏi về thói quen quá khứ: Did + S +: A question about past habits: Did + S + use to + base verb → Did you use to walk. After did, don't use "used"; "Do… used" is the wrong tense; "use to walking" is the wrong verb form.
Câu khách quan It could be argued that…: The objective sentence It could be argued that… suits academic writing. I reckon, Loads of people say and To be honest are all spoken forms.
Câu khẳng định phải dùng used (có -d). C: The affirmative needs used (with -d). Only after did/didn't do we use use to.
Câu liệt kê song song rất thường gặp ở c: Parallel list sentences are very common in Task 2 introductions and topic sentences. Comparing the wrong things is the number one error in Task 1 – always use that of / those of.
Câu mệnh lệnh phủ định khi tường thuật:: Reporting a negative command: tell sb (not) to V → told us not to use. "don't use" keeps the direct speech; "not using" and "to not using" are wrong forms.
Câu mở bài Task 1 rất hay mắc lỗi này. H: Task 1 introductions often contain this error. Check: the proportion of / the number of / the amount of → singular verb.
Câu mở bài Task 1 và Task 2 hầu như luôn: The opening sentences of Task 1 and Task 2 are almost always paraphrases of the prompt. Examiners do not count words copied from the prompt, and copying a lot lowers your Lexical Resource score.
Câu nghi vấn: dùng ít trong Writing, nhi: Interrogative: rarely used in Writing, often in Speaking
Câu quá dài, mất kiểm soát: Sentence too long, out of control
Câu tiếng Anh bắt buộc có chủ ngữ; dùng: An English sentence must have a subject; use it as a dummy subject.
Câu tiếng Anh luôn cần chủ ngữ và động t: An English sentence always needs a subject and a finite verb. Some languages can say "In Hanoi (there) are many lakes", but English must say "There are many lakes in Hanoi" or "Hanoi has many lakes".
Câu đơn, câu ghép, câu phức, câu ghép-ph: Simple, compound, complex and compound-complex sentences; exclamatory sentences (What a…! / How…!); declarative, negative, interrogative and imperative sentences. Understand why IELTS rewards "a wide range of structures" and how to combine sentence types.
Câu đầu là fragment vì không có động từ: The first sentence is a fragment because it has no main verb.
Cây cầu được xây (nghĩa bị động) → phân: The bridge was built (passive meaning) → past participle Built. Building and Having built have an active meaning (the bridge built itself); To build only expresses purpose.
With a + adjective + noun → use such.
Có danh từ (book) → dùng such a/an + adj: With a noun (book) → use such a/an + adj + N.
Có khoảng thời gian (for five years) kéo: A period of time (for five years) lasting up to a past point → use had been + V-ing instead of the past continuous.
With the article a → singular noun phenomenon. phenomena is plural; "phenomenons" and "phenomenas" are wrong forms.
Có mốc thời gian quá khứ xác định (ago): With a definite past time (ago), use the past simple, not the present perfect.
Có the employees (nhóm xác định) → most: With the employees (a specific group) → most of the employees. Most goes directly before a noun with no the; The most is a superlative; Mostly is an adverb.
Có thể giữ lại liên từ cho rõ nghĩa: whe: You can keep the conjunction for clarity: when, while, after, before, since, once, if, unless + V-ing/V3. Example: Once installed, the software updates automatically.

Dùng thì hiện tại, không dùng will: Use the present tense, not will

Dạng bị động của thức giả định là be + V: The passive form of the subjunctive is be + V3, not backshifted to was.

Dự đoán có bằng chứng ngay trước mắt → b: A prediction with evidence right in front of you → be going to. will is for opinion-based predictions; falls is present simple; "is falling to" is a wrong structure.
Dự đoán trong quá khứ về tương lai (năm: A past prediction about the future (in 1995) → would + V. will and is going to are present-time forms; has is the wrong structure.

Don't use would in the if-clause.

Không viết tắt (don't, it's, can't) tron: Don't use contractions (don't, it's, can't) in IELTS Writing; write do not, it is, cannot in full to keep a formal style.
Không đặt dấu phẩy giữa chủ ngữ và động: Don't put a comma between the subject and the verb, and don't put a comma before “that” in a noun clause: “Many people believe that…” – no comma.
Không đặt trạng từ giữa động từ và tân n: Do not place an adverb between the verb and the object.
Khả năng chung trong quá khứ → could. ca: General ability in the past → could. can is present; will be able to is future; may expresses permission/possibility, not ability.

Khả năng ở tương lai / hoàn thành (dùng: Future / completed ability (use be able to)

Kinh nghiệm tính đến một thời điểm trong: Experience up to a point in the past
Know là động từ trạng thái nên chỉ dùng: Know is a stative verb, so it takes only the present perfect, not the continuous form.
Know là động từ trạng thái, không dùng d: Know is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous form.
Kế hoạch trong quá khứ không thành → was: A past plan that did not happen → was going to. am going to and will are present/future; "was about" lacks to.
Kết hợp câu đơn thành câu phức chính xác: Combine simple sentences into accurate complex sentences while avoiding two major errors: run-on sentences and fragments.
Kết hợp hai đến ba loại mệnh đề, không q: Combine two to three types of clause, without making sentences too long
Kết hợp quá khứ – hiện tại trong câu điề: Combine past and present in mixed conditionals; use unless, provided that, as long as instead of if; and use wish / if only to express wishes and regrets.
Kết quả (vật) gây ra cảm giác ngạc nhiên: A result (a thing) causing a feeling of surprise → -ing adjective: surprising. surprised is for a person who feels surprise; surprise is a noun/verb; surprisingly is an adverb.

Kết quả của cả vế trước: Result of the whole preceding clause

A past result → would have + V3.

Let's: rủ người khác cùng làm (có cả ngư: Let's: inviting others to do something with you (the speaker is included)

Loại 2: tình huống trái với hiện tại: Second conditional: situations contrary to the present

Lùi thì khi động từ tường thuật ở quá kh: Backshift when the reporting verb is in the past
Lượng tiền, thời gian, khoảng cách → số: Amounts of money, time, distance → singular

Lỗi mạo từ là lỗi phổ biến nhất của thí: Article mistakes are among the most common errors, especially for learners whose first language has no articles. Check every singular countable noun in your writing: does it have a/an/the or another determiner?

Many/much thường dùng trong câu phủ định: Many/much are usually used in negatives and questions

Must have V3: chắc hẳn đã: Must have V3: must have done

Mệnh đề danh từ làm chủ ngữ chỉ cần một: A noun clause as subject needs only one main verb (surprised).

Mệnh đề if dùng hiện tại đơn dù nói về t: The if-clause uses the present simple even when talking about the future – many learners add will because of a time word like "tomorrow".
Mệnh đề không xác định (có dấu phẩy) dùn: A non-defining clause (with a comma) uses which, not that. that isn't used after a comma; who refers to people; what is not a relative pronoun.
Mệnh đề nhượng bộ để thể hiện lập luận c: Concessive clause to show a balanced argument

Mệnh đề thời gian (when…) chỉ tương lai: A time clause (when…) referring to the future uses the present simple, not will.
Mệnh đề thời gian bắt đầu bằng when dùng: A time clause beginning with when uses the present simple even when talking about the future. Many learners wrongly add will here.

Mệnh đề điều kiện để đưa ra giải pháp: Conditional clause to propose a solution

Mỗi đoạn thân bài nên có: một câu chủ đề: Each body paragraph should have: a clear topic sentence, a complex sentence with a concessive or conditional clause, and a sentence with a relative clause or participle phrase.
Một câu đảo ngữ hoặc câu chẻ đúng ở kết: One correct inversion or cleft sentence in the conclusion makes an essay stand out and shows wide grammatical range, but only if used accurately.
Một danh từ – hai dạng số nhiều, hai ngh: One noun – two plurals, two meanings: cloth → cloths (pieces of cloth for wiping) / clothes (garments); penny → pennies (coins) / pence (amount of money)
Một mệnh đề chính + một mệnh đề quan hệ: One main clause + one relative clause (who work part-time). A simple sentence has only one clause; a compound sentence joins two independent clauses; an imperative begins with a verb.
Một số tính từ đổi nghĩa theo vị trí: th: Some adjectives change meaning with position: the people concerned (the people involved) ≠ concerned people (worried people)
Một số từ quen thuộc tận cùng phụ âm + o: Some familiar words ending in consonant + o
Một số động từ KHÔNG đi với phản thân dù: Some verbs do NOT take a reflexive pronoun even if other languages use one: relax, feel, concentrate, meet. Say I relaxed, not I relaxed myself.

Speaking Part 3: “What I find interestin: Speaking Part 3: “What I find interesting is…”, “I do think…” make answers natural and stress the right point. Task 2: one cleft sentence in the conclusion highlights your position.

Task 1 bản đồ và biểu đồ dùng nhiều nội: Task 1 maps and charts use many intransitive verbs (rise, decline, fluctuate) and linking verbs (remain, become). Task 2 needs strong transitive verbs (reduce, tackle, raise awareness). Confusing rise/raise is a common error that loses Grammatical Accuracy marks.
Task 1 có dự báo: “It was predicted that: Task 1 has forecasts: “It was predicted that…would…”. For Speaking Part 2 about a changed plan or a decision: use was going to and was about to.
Task 1 cần so sánh liên tục: dùng trạng: Task 1 requires constant comparison: use degree adverbs (slightly, considerably, by far), multiples and rankings (the second largest) to avoid repeating "higher than".
Task 1 dạng process / map gần như bắt bu: Process / map tasks in Task 1 almost require the passive (is collected, was replaced, has been converted). In Task 2 the passive makes arguments more objective, but don't overuse it – mix it with active sentences for clarity.

Task 1 thường chấm lỗi number/amount và: Task 1 often marks number/amount and fewer/less errors. Remember: people, cars, countries → number/fewer; water, electricity, money, waste → amount/less.
Task 1 thường dùng sở hữu cách cho quốc: Task 1 often uses the possessive for countries, cities and time: the country's population, the city's residents, the UK's share, in ten years' time. It is more concise than the of structure.
Task 1 đánh giá cao việc chuyển phần tră: Task 1 rewards turning percentages into quantity phrases: 52% → a slight majority, 75% → three quarters / the vast majority, 8% → a small minority. Use the number of (countable) and the amount of (uncountable) accurately.

Task 2 thường bàn về các nhóm xã hội: th: Task 2 often discusses social groups: the elderly, the unemployed, the disabled, the homeless, the young. Task 1 often uses participles as adjectives and compound adjectives: a growing number, a declining population, a ten-year period.

Task 2: dùng loại 1 để trình bày hệ quả: Task 2: use the first conditional to present the consequences of a policy or solution. Speaking Part 3: use the zero conditional to talk about general trends in society.
Task 2: dùng so that / in order to khi đ: Task 2: use so that / in order to when proposing solutions and as a result / consequently when stating consequences – showing clear logical relationships between ideas and raising your Coherence & Cohesion score.
Task 2: dùng while / whereas để so sánh: Task 2: use while / whereas to compare two views, although / despite the fact that to concede before rebutting, owing to / due to for a formal style. Alternating clauses and noun phrases raises your Grammatical Range.
Task 2: loại 2 giúp đưa ví dụ giả định t: Task 2: the second conditional helps you give convincing hypothetical examples (If every household recycled…). Speaking Part 3 questions like "What would happen if…?" require the second conditional. Inversion (Were…/Had…) boosts your Grammatical Range score.

Thấy dấu hiệu (mệt mỏi) của một hoạt độn: Seeing evidence (tiredness) of an activity that has just been going on → have been doing. did/do don't ask about a recently ongoing activity; "are done" is wrong; "have do" is the wrong form.

The Grammatical Range and Accuracy criterion assesses both accuracy and variety. A good Task 1 answer usually uses 2–3 tenses accurately (e.g. past simple + past perfect with by), while a good Speaking Part 2 answer combines the past simple, past continuous and a present sentence as a conclusion.

Trong Speaking Part 2 (kể chuyện quá khứ: In Speaking Part 2 (telling a past story), “I was going to…, but…” and “I was just about to… when…” make the story lively and show grammatical variety.
Trong Speaking Part 2, dùng quá khứ tiếp: In Speaking Part 2, use the past continuous to set the scene before telling the main event; examiners value a flexible mix of tenses (grammatical range).
Trong Speaking, không cần dùng câu hỏi đ: In Speaking you do not need tag questions with the examiner, but a short answer + extension (Yes, I do – actually I…) gives a natural start. In Listening Section 1, tag questions are often used to confirm information – beware of answers that get corrected.
Trong Speaking, nếu chưa nghe rõ câu hỏi: In Speaking, if you did not hear a question clearly, use an indirect question: Could you tell me what you mean by "public spaces"?
Trong Speaking, đọc thiếu hoặc sai đuôi: In Speaking, missing or wrong -ed/-s endings affect both the Pronunciation and Grammatical Accuracy criteria, because the examiner cannot hear whether you used the past or the plural. Practise words often used to describe data: increased /ɪnˈkriːst/, dropped /drɒpt/, rises /ˈraɪzɪz/.
Trong Task 1, cấu trúc “…, reaching/hitt: In Task 1, the structures “…, reaching/hitting + figure” and “…, accounting for + %” link two ideas into one very natural sentence.
Trong Task 1, hầu như luôn viết “the + d: In Task 1, you almost always write “the + noun” when referring back to something in the prompt: the chart, the figure for Japan, the proportion of women. But when talking about a general trend in Task 2, omit the article: Technology has changed education.
Trong Writing Task 1 dạng biểu đồ có mốc: In Writing Task 1 charts with an end point in the past, the phrase "By + year, … had + V3" adds grammatical variety. In Speaking Part 2, use it to explain the background before the main event.
Trong Writing Task 1 dạng dự báo, will h: In Writing Task 1 projections, will have + V3 with by + year helps you avoid repeating "will increase". In Speaking Part 3, use the future continuous to picture life in the future.
Trong Writing Task 1 dạng quy trình (pro: In Writing Task 1 process diagrams, use once / after / as soon as + present perfect to link the steps. In Task 2, when predicting the future, remember: when + present.
Trong Writing Task 1 và Task 2, các danh: In Writing Task 1 and Task 2, academic nouns such as data, criteria, phenomena, analyses, the media appear frequently. Writing the correct singular/plural form and keeping verb agreement consistent improves your Grammatical Range & Accuracy score.

🌉 Hiện tại hoàn thành là \"cây cầu\" nối: 🌉 The present perfect is a "bridge" linking the past and the present. If you name a finished point in time (yesterday, in 2019, ago), the bridge is cut → switch to the past simple.
🎥 Hãy hình dung bạn đang quay video: thứ: 🎥 Imagine you are filming a video: whatever is "moving in the frame" right now takes be + V-ing. Without "be" it is like a camera with no battery – the sentence won't run!
🎧 Trong Speaking, \"nghe thì của câu hỏi: 🎧 In Speaking, "listening to the tense of the question" is the fastest way to choose the right tense: Do you…? → present simple; Did you…? → past simple; Have you ever…? → present perfect; Will…? / How might…? → future.
🎬 Quá khứ tiếp diễn là \"cảnh nền\" của: 🎬 The past continuous is the film's "background scene"; the past simple is the "sudden event". Classic pattern: While + past continuous (the long scene), when + past simple (the short event).
🏃 Đây là \"phiên bản quá khứ\" của hiện: 🏃 This is the "past version" of the present perfect continuous: simply move NOW back to a point in the past and change have been → had been.
🐍 Nhớ \"con rắn S\": chủ ngữ là he / she: 🐍 Remember the "S snake": when the subject is he / she / it or a singular noun, the verb must "wear the snake tail" -s/-es. But once does/doesn't is present, the snake moves to the auxiliary and the main verb goes back to its base form.
👀 Trước khi viết Task 1, hãy dành 10 giâ: 👀 Before writing Task 1, spend 10 seconds circling the years on the horizontal axis: all in the past → past tense; a year after the present → future; no years (process) → present simple.
📅 Hỏi nhanh ba câu: \"Vừa mới quyết định: 📅 Three quick questions: "Just decided?" → will. "Already intended?" → going to. "Already in the diary, booked, arranged with someone?" → present continuous.
📸 Quá khứ đơn giống một \"tấm ảnh đã chụ: 📸 The past simple is like a "photo already taken": the moment is closed, with a clear date or time. See ago, last, yesterday, in + year → use V2/V-ed.
🔑 Chữ \"to\" trong be/get used to là giớ: 🔑 The "to" in be/get used to is a preposition, so V-ing or a noun follows. The "to" in used to (past habit) is part of a modal-like verb, so the base form follows.
🔥 Hãy nghĩ đến \"vết tích còn nóng\": ta: 🔥 Think of "hot traces": paint on your hands, tired eyes, a sweaty shirt… When you see evidence of an activity that has just been going on for a while, use have been + V-ing.
🛫 Tưởng tượng một máy bay: \"will be fly: 🛫 Imagine a plane: "will be flying" = at that time the plane is up in the sky; "will have landed" = by then the plane has finished landing. When you see "by + future time", think of will have + V3.
🧊 Hãy coi động từ trạng thái như \"đá\": 🧊 Think of stative verbs as "ice" – still, not moving, so they can't be "…-ing". Action verbs are like "water" – they flow and move, so the continuous is fine.
🧭 Mẹo \"hai bậc thang\": đứng ở một điểm: 🧭 The "two steps" trick: stand at a point in the past and look back – the event on the lower step (the one that happened first) takes had + V3.
